status_summary: USPTO rescinded its June 2022 interim memorandum on discretionary denials on 2025-02-28, began an interim process splitting discretionary and merits institution decisions on 2025-03-26, and under a Director memorandum of 2025-10-17 has had the Director decide institution of all inter partes and post-grant reviews from 2025-10-20, usually by summary notice. It proposed rules on 2025-10-17 (90 FR 48335) that would limit inter partes review where claims were previously upheld or parallel proceedings are likely to decide validity first, extended the comment period to 2025-12-02, and no final rule appears in the Federal Register through 2026-10-18. On processing speed, the Office reported on 2026-04-10 a backlog of 776,995 unexamined applications, down from a January 2025 peak of 837,928, and on 2026-05-06 extended its fast-track appeals pilot to 2028-05-06 with a four-month decision target against average appeal pendency of about 8.5 months. Whether these changes are balanced is disputed and is not assessed here.

timeline.event: USPTO rescinds its 2022 interim procedure memorandum on discretionary denials in AIA proceedings with parallel litigation.
USPTO begins an interim process splitting institution decisions into discretionary and merits tracks, with Director decisions on discretionary issues.
USPTO publishes proposed rules limiting inter partes review for previously challenged claims or where other proceedings will likely decide validity first.
The USPTO Director issues a memorandum under which the Director decides institution of all IPR and PGR proceedings, effective 2025-10-20.
USPTO extends the comment period on its proposed inter partes review rule to 2025-12-02 (90 FR 50492) and says it does not expect further extensions.
USPTO reports 776,995 unexamined patent applications as of 2026-04-06, down from a peak of 837,928 in January 2025.
USPTO extends and modifies the fast-track appeals pilot to 2028-05-06 with a four-month decision target; average appeal pendency is reported at about 8.5 months.

title: Take a balanced approach to the PTAB and speed up application and appeal processing
uncertainties: The proposed rule (90 FR 48335, RIN 0651-AD89, docket PTO-P-2025-0025) and the 2025-11-07 extension notice (90 FR 50492) were read on federalregister.gov in review on 2026-10-18; the extension notice cites the proposal at 90 FR 48342, which may refer to a companion proposed rule on briefing discretionary denial issues that was seen in a listing but not opened. The Director memorandum of 2025-10-17 was read by the researcher and in the earlier review. A Federal Register API query of USPTO final rules since 2025-10-01 returned four rules, none on PTAB practice, and an inter partes review term query since 2025-11-01 showed no final PTAB rule. A 2026-07-22 USPTO proposed rule on real parties in interest in ex parte reexamination concerns a different proceeding and is not added. The 2026-04-10 backlog release and the 2026-05-06 pilot notice were not reopened this run. Application pendency figures were not checked. Director institution by summary notice can be read as less transparent, which cuts against the text's call for transparent processing. Court challenges to the Director's institution practice were not reviewed.
